title: Slab with temperature-dependent conductivity k ~ 1/T (analytic, Kirchhoff transform)
description:
Steady conduction through a 10 mm slab with k(T) = k_ref T_ref / T (silicon-like 1/T), x_lo held at T1 and x_hi at T2, insulated y faces (1D). The conductivity reads the heat temperature, so the stationary study iterates (Picard) until T stops changing; the sweep runs T2 over 400-1200 K.
Analytic (Kirchhoff transform, k T = const): T(x) = T1 (T2 / T1)^(x / L), so T(L/2) = sqrt(T1 T2); heat flux q = k_ref T_ref ln(T2 / T1) / L; mean T = (T2 - T1) / ln(T2 / T1) (432.8 K at T2 = 600 K, against 450 K for a constant k).
Derived values tab: q_mean (mean heat_flux_abs magnitude), T_mean and T_probe (probe at x = 50.5 dx, last fixed-point iteration), all ~1e-4 (the face conductances are harmonic means of the cell k).
Sweep tab: q_mean vs T2 with the dashed k_ref T_ref ln(T2 / T1) / L.
Probes tab: T_probe per fixed-point iteration (the convergence of the Picard loop).
Line profile tab (last sweep value, T2 = 1200 K): T_rise_profile (exponential in x) against the dashed analytic curve, plus the dashed straight line of a constant k for contrast (reported, not checked).

parameters.name: T1
